about: A canvas drawn by code (DESIGN 5.7, backend renderer). The draw handler of a canvas runs when its window opens and after every other handler of the window; each run starts an empty drawing, which the backend sends as the canvas part's `drawing`, a list of shapes in the canvas's own units (`units W x H`, 100 x 100 without it, x to the right and y down). A renderer scales the units to fit the part, keeping their proportion, centered, and draws the shapes in order. A color is a color of the theme by name (`accent`, `text`) or written out (`#rrggbb`); a name the theme does not have is its text color. Widths and sizes are in units too. `text` is centered on its point, horizontally and vertically, its text filled in the person's format like any shown text. `image` draws a picture of the project's resources folder by its name (`picture`: a .png, .jpg, .gif, .bmp, .webp or .svg file) stretched to fill its box, `x` and `y` its top left corner; a picture that is not there draws nothing. `shapes` gives the code each shape is drawn by and what it sends. `angles` gives sin and cos of degrees, rounded to 10 decimals, as every runtime computes them. A canvas can be clicked (`on click`): the renderer finds where in the canvas's units, rounded down, from where in the part the click was (clicks: the part's size and the click in pixels, the drawing fitted as it is drawn, whole and centred), sets it in the part's `pointer` and runs the handler, which reads `canvas.x` and `canvas.y` (points: a part's state and what they read, 0 without a pointer). The pointer is a record that grows: it holds `x` and `y` now, and a runtime keeps any other field it is sent without failing on it. A click beside the drawing, where the part shows none of it, runs nothing.
